From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@seastone.ai>
To: compliance@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request — post-report bridge addendum for SOC 2 Type II (report end 2026-08-31)

Hi Stephanie / Redwood compliance team,

Hope you are well — Seastone is finalizing our procurement checklist and we have one outstanding ask: a bridge addendum (management assertion or auditor-signed bridge letter) that covers the period following Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report (report period ended 2026-08-31) through today. Our procurement policy requires coverage up to the contract execution date; we are targeting a week from today for contract signature.

Specific asks:
- A one-page bridge letter or addendum stating there have been no material control changes since 2026-08-31 (or, if changes exist, a short summary and compensating controls).
- A short evidence index (control group snapshots) that maps to common SIG/SOC control areas (IAM rotations, change mgmt, incident log, uptime/patching cadence).
- If possible, KPMG-signed attestation would be best, but Seastone procurement will accept a management assertion + evidence bundle if we flag an internal risk exception.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated delivery date? If helpful, I can share the procurement template we need to attach.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security Operations
Seastone AI

Attachment: Seastone_procurement_template.pdf (referenced)

Plan proposal (please comment):
- Rishi: pull evidence index and artifacts (change mgmt snapshots, KMS rotation records, incident log summary, recent patch/maintenance windows). See attached evidence index template I drafted.
- Laura: confirm whether Legal/Finance will accept management assertion for this account; if not, advise on escalation to request an auditor addendum.
- Target: external reply to Seastone by EOD 2026-11-12 with either drafted bridge letter + evidence pack or an update on timeline for auditor-signed attestation.

I attached a draft bridge letter (Draft_Bridge_Letter-Redwood.docx) and a quick evidence index CSV for Rishi to fill. If we can get auditor sign-off, great — if not, the management assertion + documented artifacts should be sufficient to get procurement over the line with a risk exception.

Thanks — steph

Agree with sending a management assertion + evidence pack as first step. A few procurement teams will accept a management assertion if the evidence is clear; for finance/contracts, acceptance often depends on contract language and dollar threshold. Quick proposed next steps:

- I'll review the draft bridge letter and add a sentence to reference evidence index and data classification redaction approach.
- I'll ask Legal to confirm whether a procurement risk exception form will be required; if so, we should offer a 30-day post-signature remediation plan (if any findings come up).
- If Seastone insists on an auditor-signed bridge letter, we need to open a request with KPMG (cc'ed) and expect ~2–3 weeks and possible fees.

Please loop in Global Security (security@redwood.ai) on the final packet. If Sales needs the doc earlier for signature routing, we can provide a redlined management assertion with the evidence index and a short explanatory note for procurement.

- Laura
